text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic received UN administrator for Eastern Slavonia in Croatia Jacques Klein.

- Jacques Klein, head of UNTAES mission in Eastern Slavonia in Croatia, said a constructive programme is needed for return of both Serbs and Croats to where they came from in Croatia. The plan will be ready in two weeks time, he said.
- Deputy federal prime minister Danko djunic said Yugoslavia commited to reforms.
- Serbian agriculture minister Jovan Babovic said insolvency, guaranteed prices and imports are the main problems of agriculture.
- Dinar shortage topples German mark black market rate bringing it closer to the official rate of 3.3 dinars to the mark. The dinar stands at 3.5 to 3.6 to the mark.
- Montenegro preparing law on control of state security service.
- The Yugoslav Left of Montenegro says republican authorities using repressive measures to preserve personal wealth.
NASA BORBA
- Serbian oposition coalition Zajedno supports Vuk Draskovic's bid for presidency.

- Jacques Klein, UN administator in mainly Serb populated Eastern Slavonia in Croatia, says demilitarisation, dual citizenship, establishment of soft borders and return of refugees are four priorities of the UN mission in the region.

- Bosnian Foreign Minister Jadranko Prlic says succession of former Yugoslavia and Belgrade demand for Sarajevo to revoke charges against Yugoslavia before the Hague war crime tribunal for agression in 1992 are the main obstacles for normalisation of the relations between the two states.
BORBA
- Trade Union of Serbia says 51 percent of the value of capital should be distributed to workers for free in forthcoming ownership transformation.
- Representatives of electric power systems of Serbia, Montenegro, Bosnian Serb Republic, Moslem-Croat Federation and Macedonia to meet in Sarajevo April 24 to discuss cooperation.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI

- Bosnian Serb army Chief of General Staff Major-General Pero Colic says Moslems speedily arming themselves in preparation to create a Moslem state which would include Bosnian Serb Republic territory.
- Yugoslav army amnesties 7,413 draft evaders or deserters in the period to December 14, 1995.
- Croatian authorities are holding 16 Serbs in Split prison Lora for 18 months without charges or trial, says Savo Strbac, president of Veritas documentation centre.
- Yugoslav Securities Commission warns of secondary sales of regular shares of banks in over-the-counter trade at prices below their nominal value.
-- MONTENEGRO --
POBJEDA
- The Montenegrin government ordered its foreign ministry to speed up procedure for opening Greek consular office in the republic.
- Croatian water pipeline Plat to Montengrin coastal town of Herceg Novi will be under reconstruction between May 12 to June 12. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
